WHAT YOU ALREADY KNOW   What you already know
If you learned IFRS 16, you know one lessee model: every lease is like a purchase financed by a loan. U.S. GAAP keeps two models. The balance sheet looks almost the same, but the income statement and the cash flow statement can be very different.

FALSE-FRIEND ALERT   Crédit-bail is not a class
French crédit-bail and Arabic عقد تأجير تمويلي are legal forms of contract. Under ASC 842, the class depends only on the five criteria. A crédit-bail contract can be an operating lease, and an ordinary rental can be a finance lease.

WORKED EXAMPLE   Worked example: the olive-press finance lease in 2026
Step 1. Interest: 6% × $866,276 = $51,977.
Step 2. Payment of $250,000: the liability falls to $668,253.
Step 3. Amortization: $866,276 ÷ 4 years = $216,569, so the ROU asset is $649,707.
Check. Total 2026 expense is $268,546, which is $18,546 more than the payment. Figure F14-06 shows all four years.

EXAM TRAP   Measurement traps
The liability is a present value, not the total of the payments.
Each payment covers interest first; do not deduct the whole payment from the opening liability.
Operating lease: one straight-line cost; do not show interest and amortization separately.
